test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-int-005/Biolog.Features.ImportConflictReview.Tests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && bash scripts/check-module-project-references.sh && python3 scripts/check-contract-freeze.py
notes:
Round-1 FAIL (double High, both confirmed real): ZB-INT005-01 scan genuinely mutates ImportConflictReview state (raise/augment/withdraw) and writes audit events but had no provenance proof or permission check - only a forgeable X-Actor-Id header. ZB-INT005-02 list exposes exact existing-vs-incoming identity field values, person/external identifiers and decision notes with no provenance or read permission at all. Decide's own provenance+RBAC, tenant isolation/CAS and audit value-exclusion were confirmed sound - this was specifically the other two routes on this feature that got missed.

Root cause: an earlier design treated scan/list as audit-attribution-only (ADR-0006 Decision 2), borrowing BIO-INT-002's own PreviewAsync/ListBatchesAsync shape by endpoint-shape analogy without re-justifying it against THIS story's own actual side effects (scan mutates+audits; BIO-INT-002's preview never does either) or actual data sensitivity (field-level identity comparison + human notes is more sensitive than a mapping's own configuration). Same precedent-transfer-without-re-justification lesson this floor has hit before (BIO-IDN-005-AC04's own 'reusing a pattern must be re-justified for THIS story's actual data disclosure' discipline).

Fix: added ImportConflictReviewService.ReadPermission ('integrations.conflict_review_read'), checked inside the service for both ScanAsync and ListForMappingAsync (ListForMappingAsync gained an AuditActor parameter it previously lacked, needed to check the grant). Added ActorProvenanceGate.Require(context.Request, actor.Id) to both endpoint handlers (ScanAsync/ListAsync in ImportConflictReviewEndpoints.cs), mirroring DecideAsync's own existing split (permission-check-in-service, provenance-check-in-endpoint). Confirmed this exact treatment - BOTH permission and provenance required on a sensitive GET, not just the write - is the established real-codebase precedent by reading BIO-TEN-003's own TenantFeatureConfigurationEndpoints.cs directly (its GET route requires both, identical to its own PUT route) before designing, not assumed.

Upgraded FakePermissionGateway (tests/features/bio-int-005) from a single blanket grant/deny flag to per-permission-key denial (IReadOnlySet<string> deniedPermissionKeys), since scan/decide now need two independently-testable gates - a test can deny ReadPermission while still granting DecidePermission, or vice versa. Added 2 new feature tests (scan-without-read-permission, list-without-read-permission) and 2 new HTTP integration tests (provenance-required and permission-denied for both scan and list, mirroring decide's own existing pair) - 22/22 and 11/11 respectively, both up from 20/20 and 9/9.

No web/frontend change needed or made: the SIMULATION-mode mock port never modelled permission checks in the first place (same as every sibling mock in this codebase), so the Playwright proof is unaffected; the live adapter's own fetch calls are unchanged (permission enforcement is entirely server-side, transparent to the client).

Verification: dotnet build clean. Own suite 22/22 (was 20). Full Biolog.IntegrationTests 255/255 (was 253, +2 new, zero regression elsewhere). Module-reference/contract-freeze PASS. Did not re-run the full frontend/playwright suite this round since no web file changed and the backend-only diff cannot affect either (confirmed by diff scope: api/features/bio-int-005/**, tests/dotnet/**, tests/features/bio-int-005/**, docs/** only).
